evidence.detail: The class scans the exact R143 LoadoutPersistence directory for filenames beginning with the constructor-supplied loadout/folder key plus '_ver_', parses the numeric suffix and retains the highest discovered version.
The class exposes constant version 5 and initializes detected version to 1; a(int) answers whether the discovered format version is at least the requested version.
LoadoutBinaryCodec invokes the detector for versions 2, 3, 4 and 5 to conditionally decode fields added across loadout format revisions, including presentation/color/icon and later integer state.

evidence.detail: The write path serializes the R143 LoadoutDefinition name, Color, optional LoadoutIcon enum, LoadoutSpellbook, skill/config array, every LoadoutEquipmentSlot entry and inventory LoadoutItemEntry records to DataOutputStream.

The read path reconstructs LoadoutDefinition objects from DataInputStream and inserts them into the supplied R143 LoadoutFolder, recreating icons, equipment entries, inventory entries and later-version fields.
The decoder constructs rs/gui/b/b/e and uses its detected format version to gate backward-compatible fields, directly pairing this class with the loadout persistence/versioning layer.
R143 already identifies rs/gui/b/b/d as LoadoutPersistence; this class is the model-level binary codec used by that persistence subsystem rather than the filesystem owner itself.

evidence.detail: The class loads arbitrary GUI image resources from filesystem paths when running from file: Client.class URLs or from classpath resources otherwise, storing the resulting java.awt.Image.
It stores mutable x/y draw coordinates and exposes one Graphics2D draw wrapper that renders the held image at those coordinates.

Exact-v308 consumers span multiple reviewed sidebar/loadout surfaces, loading assets such as equipment slot images, skills.png, outline.png, curses.png, normal.png and many /assets/gui/icons/*.png resources.
Because the same helper is shared across loadout categories, equipment slots and other sidebar artwork, the name remains generic GuiImageAsset rather than claiming one feature-specific role.
